text:
acme-dataops: Hey team — overnight batch started getting a ton of 429s around 03:12 UTC. We’re on the free tier key (last 4: ...9f3a). This killed our ingest job. Sample error in logs:
```json
{"time":"2026-03-15T03:12:08Z","status":429,"error":"rate_exceeded","message":"Too many requests","x-request-id":"req_7c9e2"}
```
acme-dataops: We tried backing off but it’s a sustained surge from our side (heavy parallel uploads). Any temporary uplift or guidance?
maya (Support): Sorry about that — can you share the approximate QPS and typical payload size per request? Also send one X-Request-ID from a failed request (you included req_7c9e2, thx).
acme-dataops: Roughly 18 req/s at peak, ~4k tokens per request, job runs hourly for ~6 hours. We’re not intentionally retrying aggressively.
leo (Eng): On free tier we have strict per-key concurrency and token caps. 18 rps * 4k tokens ≈ 72k tokens/s — that can blow through burst windows quickly. Do you have multiple keys or a single client?
acme-dataops: single key. We assumed free tier handles short spikes.
leo (Eng): Free tier has small burst allowance and lower sustained quota. Quick repro you can run locally to simulate the issue (low risk):
```bash
for i in {1..50}; do \
  curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"input":"token-load-test","max_tokens":4000}' &
done
wait
```
leo (Eng): You should see intermittent 429s and a `retry-after` header when rate-limited. Best immediate mitigations: lower concurrency, add jittered exponential backoff, and shard across multiple API keys if you can.
maya (Support): I can open a temporary support escalation for a short burst increase, but we need authorization from billing owner and sign-off for any extended increases. Sam (Sales) — can you assist with a short-term commercial path?
sam (Sales): I can help. If they want a short paid trial we can provision a 30-day pay-as-you-go uplift; otherwise we can request a one-off +100k token/day temporary allowance while we validate patterns. Acme — are you able to take a short call or confirm billing contact?
acme-dataops: We can confirm billing contact, email is billing@acme.example. We're open to a short trial to avoid re-architecting the pipeline.
quota-bot: Automated note — free-tier token burst policy: 50k tokens/day baseline, peak grace window applies for <5 minutes. Exceptions require SRE approval.
maya (Support): Thanks. Created ticket INC-2026-3456. Requested temporary +120k tokens/day for 48 hours to validate. Pending approvals from SRE and finance.
leo (Eng): While you wait: adjust ingestion to stream smaller pieces (reduce max_tokens), enable streaming responses, and add server-side rate limiter that caps concurrent requests to 6 for now. Example Python backoff snippet: 
```python
import time, random
for attempt in range(5):
    resp = client.generate(... )
    if resp.status_code == 429:
        wait = (2 ** attempt) + random.random()*0.5
        time.sleep(wait)
        continue
    break
```
maya (Support): Action items: 1) Acme confirm billing contact (done). 2) Sales to propose trial path (Sam). 3) Eng guidance applied (Leo). 4) Support will followup on INC-2026-3456 when approvals return.
sam (Sales): Pinged billing contact with trial options and a one-click billing link. Will update here once they accept.
acme-dataops: Thanks — we'll start throttling concurrency and run the local repro to collect more X-Request-IDs. Will post logs here if the 429s persist after the config changes.
maya (Support): Closing loop for now — tracking in INC-2026-3456. Re-open thread if new failures after config changes. :thumbsup:
